s: Document-oriented NoSQL database storing flexible JSON-like BSON documents with rich query indexing and horizontal sharding.
w: Collections hold documents (BSON); schemas are dynamic by default but JSON Schema validation enforces structure. Indexes (B-tree) serve queries; aggregation pipelines compute analytics. Replica sets provide HA (primary + secondaries); sharding distributes collections across nodes by shard key. Change streams enable CDC. WiredTiger engine provides document-level concurrency.
use: Content management and catalogs with evolving schema requirements
User profiles and session stores where document shape varies by feature
Event/activity logs with flexible payload structures
Rapid prototyping where schema iteration speed matters most
avoid: Heavily relational data with many joins (PostgreSQL is stronger here)
Strict ACID multi-document transactions (supported but not optimal)
Analytical scans over billions of rows (columnar stores win)

props.shard_key: Determines data distribution - choose based on query patterns

pat.d: Writes to primary, analytics queries to secondaries or Atlas Data Lake.

pits: Unbounded document growth from array pushes - cap arrays, use bucketing pattern
Shard key miss: poor shard key creates hotspots - design from query patterns first
Multi-document transactions have performance cost - use sparingly, not by default
tips: Flexible schema is the headline advantage; mention tradeoff: flexibility vs. data integrity guarantees
Aggregation pipeline is MongoDB's answer to SQL - know $match, $group, $lookup
